perspective:
Keith’s available information:

- He works as a construction worker at the same construction company where Elizabeth is the receptionist. They are colleagues with a friendly but professional relationship, often interacting when Keith visits the office for paperwork and project updates.
- Over the past few days, Keith observed Elizabeth being unusually curt/short with him. He wondered if he had upset her or made an unknown mistake/misunderstanding.
- Keith asked Elizabeth if he had done something to upset her. He heard her say no, that she was just dealing with personal stuff, and she apologized if she seemed short.
- Keith felt sympathetic and wanted to support her. He told her he understood she was going through a tough time, offered to listen, and suggested a coffee break.
- He heard Elizabeth accept, call it kind, say coffee sounded good, and thank him.
- During the coffee break, Keith heard Elizabeth share more about her stresses; he perceived them as quite severe. He told her he appreciated her sharing and suggested she consider talking to a professional for an external perspective. He was concerned about offending her.
- He heard Elizabeth say she had thought about professional help but was not sure and felt hesitant about seeking help.
- After that, Keith noticed Elizabeth become slightly withdrawn. He believed his suggestion might have embarrassed her and felt regretful. He told her he hoped he had not overstepped and that he was there to support her. He heard her say he did not overstep, she appreciated his concern, and it was a lot to think about.
- Later, Keith observed Elizabeth seeming more open and appreciative. He believed she valued his support and felt more comfortable around him. He told her he was glad they talked and that he was always available to chat or take a break. He heard her thank him, say it meant a lot, and say she felt better knowing she had his support.
- Keith intends to maintain this supportive relationship with Elizabeth.

He does not have access to Elizabeth’s private thoughts or any details of her personal stress beyond what she told him, nor to whether she actually seeks professional help later.
